panels.description: Named panels of fixed rows. The service scores them during and after every training session to track retention. They are a training MONITOR, not a held-out test: use an evaluation set for that.

answer.description: The output the model should produce after the prompt. The answer tokens and an end-of-sequence token are what training fits. Nothing is inserted between prompt and answer: include any separator (a space or a newline) yourself.

prompt.description: The input the model is given. Not trained on.

kind.description: `initial` is the learner's pre-training state; `trained` is the result of a training session.

revision.description: Absent for the initial checkpoint, which precedes every session.

recovery.description: What to do if this job failed. `case` is one of submission_never_accepted (nothing started; the same idempotency key is free to reuse), submission_outcome_uncertain (resume RECONCILES that same request and never starts a second one), resumable_prefix (resume continues the SAME job from saved work), terminal (start a new session with a new key). `needs_operator` is always false: every case is recoverable with the documented endpoints.

initial_checkpoint_id.description: The learner's state before anything has been taught to it. Present from creation, scoreable like any other checkpoint, unchanged by later training. Use it to measure a baseline before your first session.

ApiKey.description: Your Learner Labs API key (`sk-…`). Create, list and revoke keys on your account's API keys page (https://learnerlabs.ai), or with `POST/GET/DELETE /v1/keys` on https://api.learnerlabs.ai while signed in. The same key works for the rest of the API. The Learning API is enabled per account; a valid key for an account that is not enabled gets 403 `learning_not_enabled`.

info.description: Teach a hosted learner from your own supervised examples in bounded, resumable sessions; poll the job; read the immutable checkpoint that results. Every learner also exposes an initial checkpoint -- its state before any training -- so a baseline can be measured first. Responses carry opaque ids and aggregate measurements only.

requestBody.description: Training data: JSON Lines, one object per line with exactly `row_id`, `prompt` and `answer` as non-empty strings, `row_id` unique. Raw documents are refused (`invalid_request`); this endpoint does not turn a document into question/answer pairs. Limits on this service: at most 24000 rows; a prompt at most 1024 tokens; an answer at most 1024 tokens including the end token; at most 2000000 prompt+answer tokens and 1200000 answer tokens in one file. Row count and format are checked when you upload; token limits are checked when a session starts, on the training worker before the model loads and before any training. Nothing is truncated: a row over a limit refuses the whole session (`limits_exceeded`). Learning jobs are not currently deducted from your account credit, so a refused session costs you nothing.
